//: Peak/off-peak billing windows for dspv/tkmon. Times are local to each vendor's timezone_offset_hours. `days_of_week` uses ISO weekday numbers (1=Mon .. 7=Sun); omit it to mean every day. `exceptions` are local calendar ranges billed as off-peak all day: `["YYYY-MM-DD"]` for one day, `["START", "END"]` for a start-inclusive/end-exclusive range.

vendors.name: DeepSeek
vendors.//peaks: Peak hours are 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC, Monday through Friday, excluding Chinese public holidays. All other hours are off-peak, including weekends and Chinese public holidays in full. Off-peak rates are half of peak. Source: https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing
vendors.//exceptions: Chinese public holidays, which DeepSeek bills as off-peak in full. 2026 dates from the State Council notice (国办发明电〔2025〕7号): New Year Jan 1-3, Spring Festival Feb 15-23, Qingming Apr 4-6, Labour Day May 1-5, Dragon Boat Jun 19-21, Mid-Autumn Sep 25-27, National Day Oct 1-7. Ranges are start-inclusive/end-exclusive. Only holidays from today onward are listed so this file stays readable; add earlier 2026 blocks if you are back-testing. Source: https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202511/content_7047091.htm
vendors.//exceptions-note: Statutory makeup workdays (Sep 20, Oct 10) are deliberately NOT treated as peak weekdays: they are ordinary weekends under the published rule, and pricing them as peak would overstate cost.

vendors.name: GLM
vendors.//peaks: Peak hours are Monday to Friday, 14:00-18:00 Singapore Standard Time (UTC+8). GLM-5.3 consumes plan quota at 1x off-peak and 3x peak. Sources: https://docs.z.ai/devpack/notice/usage-revision.md and https://docs.z.ai/devpack/teamplan.md
vendors.//exceptions: From September 25 to October 7, 2026 (both inclusive), all-day usage is charged at the off-peak rate. Sep 25-27 is the Mid-Autumn statutory block; the rest is z.ai's announced grace period. Source: https://docs.z.ai/devpack/notice/usage-revision.md
vendors.//rate-note: default_rate 2.0 is GLM-5.3's standing off-peak multiplier (peak 3.0 / 2), matching the documented 1x-vs-3x pair against a 2x base. The 1.0 figure advertised through September 2026 was a limited-time benefit, which is why it lives in `promotion` and expires rather than sitting in default_rate.
vendors.//promotion: 1x off-peak quota while the limited-time benefit runs. end_date 2026-10-07T16:00:00Z == 2026-10-08T00:00:00+08:00, i.e. the instant the all-day off-peak window above closes, so the two cannot disagree.
